input.quote: (i) Termination by Sanofi for Convenience. Sanofi may terminate this Agreement (A) in its entirety by providing [***] written notice of termination to RevMed or (B) on a country-by-country or Product-by-Product basis by providing [***] written notice of termination to RevMed
input.rationale: Section 12.2(a)(i) gives Sanofi (our party) an at-will termination right, exercisable both in its entirety and on a country-by-country or Product-by-Product basis, with no early-termination fee or penalty attached; Section 12.3(c) sets out only wind-down/transition consequences, and Section 12.3(c)(ii)C in fact requires RevMed to pay Sanofi post-termination royalties on Termination Products, which runs in our favour. RevMed has no reciprocal convenience right: its termination rights are limited to cause-based triggers (12.2(b) material breach, 12.2(c) insolvency, 12.2(d) Sanofi Competing Product, and 12.2(e) cessation of development, each with notice, meet-and-discuss and cure mechanics). That matches the preferred position (Customer convenience right; no Vendor convenience right during the Term). The notice periods in 12.2(a)(i) are redacted ([***]), so the exact length cannot be confirmed from the document; we should verify on the execution version that the entirety notice is workable and note that the preferred 30-day standard is unusual for a collaboration of this type. That open sub-element is noted rather than flagged.
